title_en: Xinhua Daily Press v. Nanjing Huaxia Industrial Co., Ltd. — dispute over compensation for damages from infringement of neighboring property rights
keywords_en: Civil; Neighboring Relations Tort Compensation Dispute; Second Instance; Supreme People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Legal Person; General Principles of Civil Law; Determination of Subject of Tort Liability; Whether Statute of Limitations Exceeded; Reasonableness of Damage Calculation; Affirm Original Judgment; Construction Dewatering; Ground Subsidence; Factory Building Cracking; Printing Press Damage; Principle of Fairness; Securities; Statute of Limitations
full_text_en:
Xinhua Daily Newspaper Agency v. Nanjing Huaxia Industrial Co., Ltd. — dispute over tort damages for neighboring property infringement

Plaintiff: Xinhua Daily Newspaper Agency.

Legal Representative: Liu Xiangdong, Editor-in-Chief of the agency.

Agent ad litem: Xu Yayi, Deputy Manager of the Managerial Department of the agency.

Agent ad litem: Liu Zezhen, lawyer from Nanjing First Law Firm.

Defendant: Nanjing Huaxia Industrial Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Shao Renlong, Chairman of Huaxia Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Suping, lawyer from Nanjing Financial Securities Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Xinhua Daily Newspaper Agency, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangsu High People's Court against the defendant, Nanjing Huaxia Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Huaxia Company"), regarding a dispute over tort damages for neighboring property infringement.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, during the foundation works for the Huarong Building, which it constructed at a distance of 20 meters from the plaintiff's premises, extracted and discharged a large amount of groundwater during construction, causing subsidence of the ground surface of the plaintiff's printing plant, multiple cracks in the plant's walls, displacement of the foundations of three imported and four domestic printing presses in the plant, and severe damage to the printing presses, resulting in economic losses of RMB 13.99 million. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to compensate for the losses and bear the relevant litigation costs.

Defendant's Defense: The plaintiff's losses were caused by the construction unit that carried out the foundation works of the Huarong Building, and accordingly, the construction unit should be responsible for compensation. The plaintiff's initiation of the lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations, thereby losing its right to win the case. The plaintiff's claims should be handled by administrative departments. The defendant requested that the plaintiff's claims be dismissed.

The Jiangsu High People's Court, upon trial, found the following facts: The Huarong Building, invested in and constructed by the defendant Huaxia Company, is adjacent to the plaintiff, Xinhua Daily Newspaper Agency. On January 15, 1991, Nanjing Huaxia Real Estate Development and Construction Co., Ltd. (later renamed "Huaxia Company"), a joint venture between Nanjing Real Estate Development Corporation and Hong Kong Dunheng Investment Co., Ltd., was formally established. In April of the same year, the foundation works for the Huarong Building, invested in and constructed by the company, commenced in accordance with a construction plan reviewed and approved by the defendant and relevant units. Approximately one month later, ground subsidence was discovered near the construction site, and construction was halted. On June 15 of the same year, the defendant and relevant units reviewed and approved a revised construction plan, and the foundation works resumed. In mid-October, Xinhua Daily discovered cracks in the walls and floor of its printing plant, abnormalities in its three German-made offset printing presses, a significant decline in newspaper printing quality, severe damage to the printing presses, and damage to the plant walls posing a risk to personnel safety. In response, the Nanjing Municipal People's Government dispatched personnel to convene relevant units and experts for discussion. After remedial measures were taken, the ground subsidence of the Xinhua Daily printing plant was effectively controlled, but the damage to the plant and printing presses was not addressed. Appraisals conducted by the Nanjing Civil and Architectural Engineering Society, the National Printing Machinery Quality Supervision and Inspection Center, and the Seismological Bureau of Jiangsu Province, commissioned by Xinhua Daily, concluded that the direct cause of the damage to the Xinhua Daily printing plant and the printing presses therein was the large-scale extraction and discharge of groundwater during the foundation works of the Huarong Building. On July 10, 1992, Xinhua Daily reported the matter to the Nanjing Municipal People's Government, requesting that Huaxia Company compensate for the losses, but the issue was not resolved. Xinhua Daily then directly sought compensation from Huaxia Company, but negotiations were unsuccessful. On June 30, 1994, Xinhua Daily filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting that Huaxia Company compensate for property losses.

Upon investigation: 1. The losses already incurred by Xinhua Daily were as follows: expenses for inviting domestic and foreign experts to adjust and repair the printing presses: RMB 179,504; difference in expenses for having others print part of the newspapers during the period when experts were repairing and adjusting the printing presses: RMB 31,893.50; accommodation and meal expenses for German experts coming to Nanjing to repair the printing presses: RMB 6,796.40; appraisal fee for the Nanjing Civil and Architectural Engineering Society: RMB 3,000; appraisal, evaluation, transportation, accommodation, and meal expenses for the National Printing Machinery Quality Supervision and Inspection Center: RMB 18,100 in total; consulting and appraisal fees for other relevant units: RMB 47,600. 2. Losses that Xinhua Daily would inevitably continue to incur were as follows: purchase cost of necessary parts for repairing the imported printing presses: RMB 7.65 million; customs duties and value-added tax payable on the purchase of those parts: RMB 2.44 million; costs for dismantling, transporting, storing, installing, and calibrating the printing presses: RMB 1.9 million; engineering costs for repairing and reinforcing the plant and redoing the printing press foundations: RMB 1,506,686.38. The plaintiff's total losses, both already incurred and to be incurred, amounted to RMB 13,883,580.28.

The above facts are confirmed by the statements of both parties, relevant witness testimony, appraisal conclusions, engineering budget documents, receipts, and other evidence. After cross-examination in court, the defendant did not request a new appraisal regarding the appraisal conclusions and evaluation budgets made by the departments commissioned by the plaintiff.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held: The Huarong Building constructed by the defendant Huaxia Company is adjacent to the printing plant of the plaintiff Xinhua Daily. When constructing the Huarong Building, Huaxia Company failed to fully consider the safety of the neighboring building. During construction, it extracted and discharged a large amount of groundwater, and after discovering the initial problems, failed to take necessary protective measures in a timely manner. This caused subsidence of the ground surface of the Xinhua Daily printing plant, damaged the plant's foundation, and resulted in damage to the plant and the printing machinery therein. The facts are clear and the evidence is sufficient to establish this. Huaxia Company, in constructing the building, violated the provisions of Article 83 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, which states: "In handling neighbouring relations in respect of water diversion, drainage, passage, ventilation, lighting, etc., the neighbouring parties to an immovable property shall act in the spirit of helping production, making life convenient, unity and mutual assistance, and fairness and reasonableness." Huaxia Company caused enormous losses to Xinhua Daily and shall bear full liability for compensation. The constructed Huarong Building is owned by Huaxia Company, and the damage to Xinhua Daily's printing plant and printing presses was caused by the extraction of groundwater during the foundation works of Huaxia Company's building. As for the disputes between Huaxia Company and the construction unit, these constitute another legal relationship and are not adjudicated in this case. Therefore, the defendant's argument that "the construction unit should be liable for compensation" is not accepted. After Xinhua Daily's rights and interests were infringed, it reported the matter to the Nanjing Municipal People's Government on July 30, 1992, and continuously sought compensation from Huaxia Company without resolution, until it filed a lawsuit with the court on June 30, 1994. This is in compliance with Article 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, which provides: "The period of limitation for filing a lawsuit with a people's court to protect civil rights is two years." The lawsuit was not filed beyond the statutory limitation period. Huaxia Company's argument that "Xinhua Daily's initiation of the lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations, thereby losing its right to win the case" cannot be sustained. As for Xinhua Daily's other losses, as they were voluntarily waived, they are not affirmed. Accordingly, on November 28, 1994, the court rendered the following judgment:

Huaxia Company shall, within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Xinhua Daily for all losses totaling RMB 13,883,580.28.

Court costs for this case: RMB 79,428; preservation costs: RMB 70,520; totaling RMB 149,948, to be borne by Huaxia Company.

Huaxia Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Supreme People's Court, with the following grounds: The design and use of the appellee's offset printing workshop were unreasonable; no sand and gravel cushion layer was laid under the offset printing press foundations; and no settlement observation records were made after the offset printing presses were in operation. Therefore, it could not be proven that the uneven settlement was caused solely by the groundwater extraction during the Huarong Building construction. Huaxia Company requested the reversal of the first-instance judgment and, upon clearly determining the degree of liability of each party and reasonably calculating the appellee's losses, a modified judgment apportioning civil liability between both parties.

Xinhua Daily argued in its defense that the facts found by the original trial were entirely consistent with reality. The cause of the damage to its plant and machinery was entirely the long-term, large-scale extraction and discharge of groundwater during the Huarong Building construction. It requested that the original judgment be affirmed and the appellant's appeal be dismissed.

The Supreme People's Court held: In constructing the Huarong Building adjacent to the appellee Xinhua Daily's plant, the appellant Huaxia Company should have fully considered the safety of the adjacent building. However, the company violated the principles of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC regarding the handling of neighboring relations. It commenced open excavation without first implementing protective engineering works and extracted and discharged large quantities of groundwater. Although remedial measures were taken after the initial problems were discovered, they failed to completely prevent uneven settlement. This caused subsidence of the ground surface of Xinhua Daily's printing plant and equipment foundations, resulting in severe damage to the plant and offset printing presses. Therefore, Huaxia Company shall bear full responsibility for this. Regarding the grounds of appeal raised by the appellant, during the trial of this case, upon the appellant's application, this court commissioned the Jiangsu Provincial Technical Supervision Construction Engineering Quality Inspection Station (hereinafter referred to as the "Quality Inspection Station") to conduct an appraisal on issues such as the impact of groundwater extraction during the Huarong Building construction on the Xinhua Daily printing workshop plant and imported offset printing press foundations. The Quality Inspection Station's appraisal concluded that the large-scale extraction and discharge of groundwater during the Huarong Building construction was the direct cause of the subsidence and cracking of Xinhua Daily's offset printing workshop and the inability of the offset printing presses to operate normally, as well as the resulting damage. In response to the appellant's assertion that there were problems with the design and use of the Xinhua Daily plant foundations and equipment foundations, the appraisal concluded: "The structural types of the plant foundations and equipment foundations are sensitive to settlement and have poor adaptability to environmental changes. However, no problems were found during three years of use prior to the incident. Had no groundwater extraction occurred during the foundation pit construction of the Huarong Building, this incident would not have suddenly occurred." Therefore, the facts found by the court of first instance were clear, and the law applied was correct. The appellant's grounds of appeal cannot be sustained. Accordingly, on May 13, 1996, the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

Court costs for the second instance: RMB 79,428; appraisal fees: RMB 232,751.70, both to be borne by the appellant Huaxia Company.
